thread:
sam: Quick sync on GA acceptance criteria for the launch next month.

Key ask: we need a compact "go/no-go" checklist that ties SLA wording, penalty language, monitoring coverage, and support expectations to a binary acceptance decision. Who wants to own the checklist doc?

ravi: I can take the checklist owner role. Suggest we separate two flows: pilot customers (contracted) vs self-serve GA customers. Different SLA expectations.

tess: +1. For pilot customers we should include an explicit escalation timeline (15m ack for P0, 1h remediation steps), while GA self-serve should have best-effort 24/7 paging for platform-wide incidents only. We need this in the support table.

marco: Eng note: SLA metrics we can commit to at GA: 99.8% regional uptime for hosted API, 95p latency under 400ms for single-sequence requests (baseline). Anything stronger needs extra Dedicated capacity commits.

sam: Good. Ravi, can you map those numbers into concrete SLA phrasing (credits formula + exceptions)? We need legal sign-off.

ravi: Will draft. Two design choices to flag: (A) offer latency in SLOs vs availability-only SLA; (B) include force-majeure & planned maintenance carve-outs. My preference: availability SLA + SLO latency targets in docs (non-binding) to avoid complex credit calculations.

legal: We prefer deterministic credit math if SLA is binding. If you go availability-only, credits are simpler (monthly credit % for downtime bands). If latency is binding, expect longer legal review. Also we need to flag data residency notes for Private customers in the SLA.

tess: Ops: for monitoring readiness, we require per-tenant error-rate dashboards, end-to-end smoke tests, and a synthetic token-usage check running every 5m. I'll own the smoke tests.

marco: For runbooks: we need clear rollback criteria for model rollouts (quality regression detector) and an automated fallback path to a smaller model variant to keep availability in degraded modes. I'll add the fallback config to the rollout playbook.

sam: Docs readiness: what do we consider "complete"? Minimal: public API spec, rate limits, error codes, best-practices. Bonus: example integration guides for Node/Python and an embed cost calculator. Maya from devex offered to write integration guides; we should link them.

ravi: Pricing readiness: must include a validated cost model (tokens->$) and a clear pilot-to-GA migration path with billing proration. We also need quotas and soft-limits to prevent runaway invoices.

tess: Support readiness: propose a T-shirt sizing table mapping incident severity -> support route (chat, pager, CS phone). For top-tier pilots we require named support contacts and weekly syncs during the first month. I'll put a template in the support playbook.

ops-bot: runbook-checker: smoke-tests scheduled (cron every 5m). Alerting burn-in job created (ID: RB-889).

sam: Action items summary (owners + due):
- ravi: SLA draft w/ credit calc OR availability-only option (ETA 3 days)
- legal: quick review of SLA options (ETA 4 days)
- tess: smoke tests + support T-shirt table (ETA 2 days)
- marco: fallback model config + rollback criteria (ETA 3 days)
- maya: integration guides stub (ETA 5 days)
- ravi & finance: cost validation matrix (ETA 5 days)

sam: Also, let's bake a simple acceptance test that the release board can run: 1) synthetic request throughput test (50 RPS, 5m) 2) end-to-end correctness check against a small prompt set. Pass/fail decides GA readiness.

marco: I'll commit the k8s job for the throughput test and add a small harness. Command we can run: `kubectl run ga-throughput --image=loadgen:stable -- k6 run --vus 50 --duration 5m burst.js`.

ravi: I'll add the acceptance test to the release pipeline as a gating step.

sam: No objections voiced. If all owners hit ETAs we'll reconvene in 1 week to sign off. Thanks.
